title: Memory Compass: GPU tiling, KV placement and activation headroom guidance for mixed-batch inference
creator: Sophie Martinez
description: Design and implement a reproducible GPU memory budgeting model (the 'Memory Compass') that produces conservative but cost-effective headroom reservations per-GPU across three memory classes: model weights, KV cache working set, and transient activations. This ticket covers the specification, allocator hooks, telemetry additions, and a staged rollout with load tests to validate eviction rates and latency regressions for mixed-batch inference workloads.
background: We routinely see memory storms when mixed-batch traffic with large-prefetch KV access patterns coincides with weight uploads/replicas and short-lived activation peaks (long context + many parallel requests). Existing heuristics are ad-hoc per-release and have led to 503s during regional spikes (incident-2025-09-kv-eviction). We need a portable algorithm that: (1) expresses budget components in percentile terms, (2) exposes knobs to trade cost vs. availability, and (3) plugs into the runtime slab allocator and scheduling planner.
goals: 1) Define a compact budget formula that sums weights, KV working set percentile, and activation tail + configurable margin; 2) Implement allocator quota hooks that surface per-tenant and per-GPU headroom corridors; 3) Add telemetry and Grafana panels for per-GPU budget vs. actual; 4) Run chaos/load tests to verify <1% eviction at p99 load with default margin.
proposed_solution: Introduce 'Memory Compass' which computes a per-GPU reserve using: reserve = weights + kv_p95 + activations_p99 * activation_factor + static_margin. Components: - weights: deterministic footprint per model version (from model-info registry) - kv_p95: sliding-window 95th percentile of active KV pages per-tenant weighted by request concurrency - activations_p99: modeled from request sequence-length distribution and batching profiles (sampled) - activation_factor: compensates for batching variability (default 1.15) - static_margin: site-configurable headroom (default 0.06 * gpu_total_memory) Implementation: - New telemetry probes in allocator to export kv working set percentiles, activation estimate, and computed reserve. - Allocator hook enforces soft-reserve: allow transient overshoot up to soft_watermark but trigger preemptive batching/eviction recommendations when soft->hard threshold crossed. - Scheduler uses reserve to decide placement and request admission (prefer placing new heavy models on GPUs with reserve headroom). - New admin API to simulate reserves for given workload profiles.
tradeoffs: Conservative reserves reduce throughput and increase cost; aggressive settings risk evictions and 5xxs. Choosing percentiles (p95/p99) trades sensitivity vs. stability. Complexity increase in allocator code path and added telemetry overhead (small, ~2-3% CPU). We favor default conservative settings and provide runtime knobs per-customer/tenant for Dedicated mode. For Hosted, we will start with stricter defaults and a 2-week evaluation window before relaxing.
rollout_plan: 1) Spec review and sign-off (owners: Ravi, Sophie) - 1 week; 2) Implement telemetry and reserve calculator (branch) - 2 weeks; 3) Integrate soft-reserve enforcement in allocator behind a feature flag - 1 week; 4) Canary in staging with synthetic mixed-batch load (use loadtest-suite A/B) - 3 days; 5) Promote to limited production (small tenant cohort) and monitor dashboards for 7 days; 6) Gradual ramp to all hosts over 72 hours with auto-rollback on eviction spikes > 1%. All code merged under feature flags. See playbook links for runbook steps.
metrics:
- p95 KV eviction rate per host (target < 0.5%)
- p99 request latency delta after rollout (target < +10ms)
- GPU memory utilization tail (p99) vs reserve (target reserve >= observed p99)
- incidence of forced model unloads (target 0)
- cost delta on Dedicated fleet (monitor weekly)
acceptance_criteria: 1) Reserve calculator implemented and unit-tested; 2) Telemetry gaps closed: kv_p95, activations_p99, computed_reserve exported; 3) Staging loadtest shows <0.5% eviction at p95 and latency regressions within targets; 4) Feature-flagged rollout validated on 5% of production hosts with no customer-visible errors for 7 days; 5) Documentation and admin simulation UI available in Console; 6) PRs reviewed and approved by runtime and infra leads.
